Non-canonical & suspected-error multi-addresses 2,862

Source: C:\Users\kk\Code\toronto-2-address-import\data\osm\toronto-addresses.json · ← back to summary

Every addr:housenumber in the clipped extract that either uses a non-canonical multi-value separator (,, /, N-M) or looks like a data-entry error (reversed ranges, huge spans, mixed separators). Canonical ;-separated values are excluded. Click any row to open it on osm.org.

Pick a verdict per row and click Save & export. Actionable verdicts (→ ,, unit-#, reverse) are re-checked against live Overpass before being written to a JOSM-ready .osm file. → , rewrites the housenumber using , as the list separator — it's non-canonical per OSM wiki, but ~2.5× more common than ; in this dataset.

`N-M` where N ≥ M. Almost certainly data-entry errors.

Mixed separators warn 0

A single tag combines two or more of `;`, `,`, `/` (non-fraction). Tokenizers that split on only one separator will misread these.

no entries in this category

Range-style with letter suffix warn 11

e.g. `2523A-2539A`, `567-567A`. Readable to a human but non-standard for machines.
